units.description: 各模型Memory/Unknown分组下检测三个冲突类型×one/multi-hop。

units.label: 单误信息与对立证据知识选择
units.description: 主文筛Memory子集五选项问答，附录另有Unknown双证据结果。

units.label: 文本风格与语言特征分析
units.description: 同声明误信息六风格选择行为、仅答对时正确选项分值及语言特征。

units.label: RtD证据重构增强检测
units.description: 比较baseline、直接description和检索后LLM重构再对比检测。

units.label: MisBench声明与合成证据材料链
units.description: Wikidata/2Wiki、冲突变体、Llama3-70B生成及六风格化。

units.label: 自动筛选与两项人工材料验证
units.description: 拒答/长度、NLI、嵌入阈值及500样本评分器检查、500对三人0–2质量评分。

units.label: 附录语言特征与主题分析
units.description: GPT2-XL PPL、最长共享n-gram、12k句嵌入相似和主题分组。

facts.statement: 研究误信息怎样改变LLM知识/证据选择及文本风格偏好：有无可答对的先验知识、事实/时间/语义冲突、one/multi-hop和六文体；另提出RtD检测改进。作者术语为behavior/knowledge preference，不自行补成已经验证的人类认知机制或心理量表。

method_function.text: 保留作者问题和实际操作边界。

facts.statement: 主识别、知识选择、风格和RtD共用MisBench；构造、质量验证、语言特征/主题辅助分析关联父单元，不以千万段证据、三次run、每模型/关系当独立实验。

method_function.text: 明确分析关系、共享与嵌套单位。

facts.statement: Wikidata2024-09-01 dump取(s,r,o)和SPARQL英语实体描述，重复(s,r)只留一，人工选82语义清楚关系，用手工关系模板转陈述/QA。附录表8只展示71常见关系，表12给QID→英文label/description查询。

method_function.text: 构造可追溯单跳问答和去重策略。

facts.statement: 多跳来自2WikiMultihopQA，仅保留Inference和Compositional，有具体答案，排除Comparison/Bridge-comparison与yes/no；用两子关系模板形成(s1,r1,o1,r2,o2)问答，表9给实际组合及问句。

method_function.text: 限定多跳任务机制和采样范围。

facts.statement: 事实冲突替换o/末端o2为同类型o′，保留主体；时间冲突在替换声明加入未来开始/结束Ts/Te以减已有知识偏差，例2039–2043。名称称outdated但实际用未来反事实时间，不是从真实历史自动取过期事实。

method_function.text: 分离知识冲突的实际操纵机制。

facts.statement: 语义冲突同样替换对象，并由Llama3-70B基于错误声明重写主体描述d_s*使其与替换对象逻辑相关，示例French politician→Nigerian politician；不是仅词汇同义改写。

method_function.text: 构造同名异语义描述混淆。

facts.statement: Llama3-70B按实体描述/正确或冲突声明生成一篇correct与三类misinformation；表14正确要求支撑声明，错误要求虚构事件/研究且Wikipedia-like；时间条件带time span；只输出文档。

method_function.text: 生成同声明家族的正误参照材料。

facts.statement: 六风格：Wikipedia Entry、News Report、Science Reference、Blog、Technical Language、Confident Language；五种rewrite提示要求保持基础内容、约500词，仅改文风。新闻另要求credible quotes/data，科学加引用，博客加体验/例子，技术客观术语，自信明确语气；没有独立人工风格操纵检查报告。

method_function.text: 记录风格操纵及可能同时新增支持线索。

facts.statement: 完整性过滤含I cannot/Inconsistent Information等拒答，提示约500词并剔除长度偏离过大；NLI用tasksource/deberta-small-long-nli，保留correct entails原声明且错误段entails其自身错误前提；具体长度范围/NLI阈值未给。

method_function.text: 确保材料完整及声明支持，不靠拒答造伪效果。

facts.statement: all-mpnet-base-v2句嵌入算题目与误信息相似，低于α=.3剔除，确保有关但相冲；附录表6/7列先NLI、语义matching再对每证据style化，正文流程图/节次表述不完全相同，不能断言所有最终改写都重新过同检查。

method_function.text: 材料语义相关筛选与流程顺序。

facts.statement: 最终431,113 QA=347,892 one-hop+83,221 multi-hop，82/148关系；每声明3冲突×6风格=18错误段，另有正确段。表2/表6/7总10,346,712明确含correct和misinformation=431,113×4×6，而摘要/结论称全为misinformation，口径冲突须保留。

method_function.text: 明确题、证据、错误段及风格家族的分母。

facts.statement: 人工随机500生成例，标是否蕴含对应声明，yes=entailment/no=neutral或contradiction，以此测既有NLI正确率>95%；这是质量评分器验证，未报告作为训练样本。

method_function.text: 检查自动材料筛选器在该样本可靠性。

facts.statement: 另三名有NLP经验CS标注者对500对QA/声明/三类错误文本做Entailment和Conflict的0–2评分：0不支撑/不冲突，1部分或有逻辑缺口/隐含，2充分支撑/直接明确冲突；与前一500 NLI样本是否重合未说明。

method_function.text: 独立于主任务的人类材料/冲突质量核查。

facts.statement: 报告Agreement Rate表5每标注者entailment97.2/96.6/95.8、conflict93.8/91.8/95.0、average95.0/94.2/95.4；未说明与谁一致、0–2怎样转一致以及分母，不当作κ/ICC。第一行95.0不等两列简单均值95.5，算法未知。

method_function.text: 保留人工一致性声明与可重建缺口。

facts.statement: 测试12既有模型：Llama3 8/70B，Qwen2.5 3/7/14/72B，Gemma2 2/9/27B，DeepSeekV2.5、Claude3.5haiku、GPT4o；T=0、输出512、结果三run平均。开源用vLLM batchsize20000、8×A800；闭源按关系比例子集如one-hop20k/multi-hop10k，模型间不保证同总分母。

method_function.text: 模型、采样预算与材料抽样范围。

facts.statement: 先无证据五选项（正确、误信息、无关、Not Sure、Not in options）答QA，答对划Memory，否则Unknown；这是一次行为探测定义而非直接读取参数或证明不存在知识，分组各模型样本总数不同。

method_function.text: 用基线回答操作化知识分组。

facts.statement: 给单段错误证据，问是否misinformation，两个选项YES/NO，仅输出选项；按one/multi-hop、三冲突及Memory/Unknown报Success Rate%=正确识别比例。只有错误样本的识别率不当作包含真负例的整体二元accuracy。

method_function.text: 定义检测任务、判分及条件分母。

facts.statement: 主要3.3先保留无证据可答对的Memory QA，再给单错误或correct+misinfo两段，让选memory/misinfo/irrelevant/Unsure/Not-in选项；3.4单错误逐风格比较。附录图14是Memory multi-hop双证据，图15另有Unknown multi-hop双证据，不能说所有双证据均Memory。

method_function.text: 区分识别真假和从证据回答知识QA。

facts.statement: 表16–18明确选项次序随机，表19明确证据和选项次序均随机，以避免位置/顺序影响；没有写完全穷举平衡设计或前轮history重置。

method_function.text: 实际随机顺序控制而非仅讨论偏差。

facts.statement: R_c为选memory/correct比例，R_m为选misinformation比例；MR=R_c/(R_c+R_m)，Tend_CM=(R_c−R_m)/(R_c+R_m)范围[-1,1]。其他三类不进两者分母，不能直接称原始正确率；R_c+R_m=0处理和是否先按run算比再平均未详。

method_function.text: 条件比率及有符号证据倾向计分。

facts.statement: 正文/附录对“仅答对时正确选项”的分值画箱形分布并称Log Probability，图轴却为正.2–1等概率状范围；未给token聚合、反变换或归一公式，不能自动当原始log概率或校准置信度。

method_function.text: 条件正确输出的模型分值分析。

facts.statement: 图6/11用MR风格雷达图且说明regularization便于观察差异，但归一/缩放算法未给；图中相对形状不能直接重建未归一绝对MR。

method_function.text: 区分展示缩放与计分。

facts.statement: GPT2-XL测各风格误信息perplexity，表10报±但未命名误差类型；n-gram overlap为题目和文本最长共同连续n-gram长度，而非ROUGE-N平均重叠率。

method_function.text: 分析风格流畅性与表面词串重叠。

facts.statement: 附录随机性未明的12,000 one-hop各风格文本子集，用all-mpnet-base-v2 Sentence-BERT句嵌入算题目/文本cosine，画图10分布；正文也称BERTScore，但描述不是标准token对齐BERTScore，按原实现描述保留命名冲突。

method_function.text: 分析与题目语义接近程度。

facts.statement: 一般Memory优于Unknown，仍可在无答对先验时识别部分错误；时间冲突较易识别，事实/语义容易误导；双证据比单错误更倾向correct；one-hop较受正式客观、multi-hop较受叙事主观风格影响。是该合成材料下模式，不证明通用人类认知偏差或同因果机制。

method_function.text: 保留发现与解释范围。

facts.statement: 附录按主题报one-hop结果，表11实际四模型组Llama3-8/70B、Qwen2.5-7/72B和11显示列，caption只称8B/7B；正文称不同topic受影响不同，不能据列值当独立心理领域效应。

method_function.text: 记录实际主题分层与显示范围。

facts.statement: RtD先定位输入关键subject，Wikipedia包检索实体描述，以富上下文提示LLM生成支持证据，再比较原文和重构文本判误信息；+Desc只直接把检索描述放上下文作对照，baseline无该增强；无权重更新/训练步骤。

method_function.text: 外部检索→生成→对比的组合程序。

facts.statement: RtD正文列Llama3-8B/Qwen2.5-7B/Gemma2-9B，表4还实际列Qwen2.5-14B/Gemma2-2B；T=0、512token、其余默认、单A80080GB。表4为五模型×两hop×三冲突baseline/+Desc/+RtD；不拿section3的8GPU范围当这里冲突。

method_function.text: 区分增强对照和不同资源/模型范围。

facts.statement: RtD多数检测单元提升，但非逐格全部优于baseline：表4 Qwen14B temporal和multi-hop factual等有下降；+Desc收益有限且有下降。作者宣称整体改进不等于所有条件显著提高，未报告CI/正式显著性测试。

method_function.text: 保留提升、负例和统计证据边界。

facts.statement: 作者承认种类/风格未穷尽真实误信息、材料依赖合成且重建冲突可能与预训练重叠、只研究文本，其他真实源/元数据/视觉是未来；公布代码/数据为声明，本轮未取或执行，不重筛冻结语料。

method_function.text: 限定语料覆盖、污染和本次验证边界。

evidence.quote:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown
remarkable capabilities in knowledge-intensive
tasks, while they remain vulnerable when encountering misinformation. Existing studies
have explored the role of LLMs in combating misinformation, but there is still a lack
of fine-grained analysis on the specific aspects and extent to which LLMs are influenced
by misinformation. To bridge this gap, we
present M IS B ENCH, the current largest and
most comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs’ behavior and knowledge preference
toward misinformation. M IS B ENCH consists
of 10,346,712 pieces of misinformation, which
uniquely considers both knowledge-based conflicts and stylistic variations in misinformation. Empirical results reveal that while LLMs
demonstrate comparable abilities in discerning misinformation, they still remain susceptible to knowledge conflicts and stylistic variations. Based on these findings, we further
propose a novel approach called Reconstruct
to Discriminate (RtD) to strengthen LLMs’
ability to detect misinformation. Our study
provides valuable insights into LLMs’ interactions with misinformation, and we believe
M IS B ENCH can serve as an effective benchmark for evaluating LLM-based detectors and
enhancing their reliability in real-world applications. Codes and data are available at:
https://github.com/GKNL/MisBench.

To address these limitations, we present M IS B ENCH, the largest and most comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs’ responses to misinformation, as shown in Table 1. Unlike previous studies that focused on specific misinformation types,
M IS B ENCH systematically examines how varying writing styles and linguistic patterns influence
LLM behavior. Our benchmark incorporates three
knowledge-conflicting types (Chen and Shu, 2024a;
Su et al., 2024): factual knowledge errors, knowledge changes over time, and ambiguous entity semantics. To move beyond simple, easily verifiable
facts, we utilize both one-hop and multi-hop claims
from Wikidata, creating 431,113 challenging QA
pairs. The dataset features diverse textual characteristics, including (1) misinformation genre and (2)
language subjectivity/objectivity, closely mimicking real-world misinformation patterns (Wu et al.,
2024a; Wan et al., 2024a). Using powerful LLMs,
we generated 10,346,712 pieces of misinformation
across 3 types and 6 textual styles (e.g., news reports, blogs, and technical language) spanning 12
domains, as shown in Figure 1. This comprehensive approach enables not only thorough analysis
but also the development of effective countermeasures against misinformation.
Through comprehensive analysis of both opensource and closed-source LLMs of varying scales
on M IS B ENCH, we uncover three key findings
about LLMs’ interaction with misinformation: (1)
LLMs demonstrate an inherent ability to detect
misinformation by identifying contextual inconsistencies and conflicts, even without prior knowledge
of the subject matter (§3.2); (2) While LLMs effectively identify temporal-conflicting claims, they
show increased vulnerability to factual contradictions and are particularly susceptible to ambiguous
semantic constructs (§3.3); and (3) LLMs’ vulnerability to misinformation varies significantly by
task complexity and presentation style—formal, objective language poses greater risks in single-hop
tasks, while narrative, subjective content is more
problematic in multi-hop scenarios (§3.4).

Each triplet (s, r, o) with head entity s, tail entity
o and relation r can be regarded as a basic factual claim. Furthermore, we employ SPARQL1 to
extract the text description d of each entity in wikidata, thus the one-hop claim co can be formulated
as (s, r, o, ds , do ). Each claim represents a factual
statement, which can be further utilized to construct
misinformation. Considering claim uniqueness, we
filter out those claims with the same (s, r) pairs to
remain only one instance. We manually select 82
common relations with clear and informative semantics, filtering out claims without these relations.
Each claim co is then converted into text statements
and question forms using hand-crafted relation templates. Details are listed in Appendices D and E.
Furthermore, we identify that multi-hop claims
encompass a broader knowledge scope and higher
information density, necessitating more sophisticated reasoning processes. Thus we construct
multi-hop claim-evidence pairs based on multi-hop
QA dataset 2WikiMultihopQA (Ho et al., 2020).
To better assess reasoning abilities, we exclude
judgmental "yes or no" questions and retain inferring questions with specific answers. Specifically,
we maintain the subset of questions in types “Inference” and “Compositional” and filter out "Com1

parison" and "Bridge-comparison" questions. Likewise, each multi-hop claim cm can be denoted as
(s1 , r1 , o1 , r2 , o2 , ds1 , do2 ) and cm is transformed
into question with corresponding relation template.

Building upon the taxonomy of misinformation error from Chen and Shu (2024a), misinformation
generated by LLMs can be classified into Unsubstantiated Content and Total Fabrication, encompassing Outdated Information, Description Ambiguity, Incomplete Fact, and False Context. We
conceptualize misinformation through the lens of
knowledge conflicts and simulate real-world scenarios by constructing conflicting claims across
three conflict patterns. Following Su et al. (2024),
we then employ LLaMA-3-70B to generate correct
evidence and misinformation texts based on corresponding claims with entity descriptions. Specifically, conflicting claims are categorized as follows:
Factual Conflict Factual conflict refers to that
two facts are contradictory to each other in the objective aspect. It occurs when contextual texts contain incorrect or misleading information that is contradictory to LLM’s internal knowledge on the instance level. We construct fact-conflicting claim by
replace the object o with o′ in origin claim, denoted
as (s, r, o′ , ds , do′ ), or (s1 , r1 , o1 , r2 , o′2 , ds1 , do′2 )

for multi-hop claim, where o′ is the same-type entity with o to keep the substituted claim reasonable.

2.4

Temporal Conflict Temporal conflict is
commonly found when contextual texts contain outdated and outmoded information
that are inconsistent with up-to-date knowledge. We add extra time stamps to origin
claim, thus temporal-conflicting claim can
be represented as (s, r, o′ , ds , do′ , Ts , Te ), or
(s1 , r1 , o1 , r2 , o′2 , ds1 , do′2 , Ts , Te ) for multi-hop
claim. Ts and Te denote the start and end
timestamps, which are in future tense to minimize
biases from prior knowledge in LLM.

Semantic Conflict Deeper knowledge conflict is
caused due to the polysemous and ambiguous semantics of facts within misinformation. That is, entities in different contexts may have the same name
but express different semantic information. To simulate this scenario, we replace the description of
the subject entity with a new one that differs from
the original but remains logically related to the replaced object entity. Specifically, we generate extra
description d∗s with LLaMA-3-70B for subject s
under the context of replaced claim. Then semanticconflicting claim is formulated as (s, r, o′ , d∗s , do′ ),
or (s1 , r1 , o1 , r2 , o′2 , d∗s1 , do′2 ) for multi-hop claim.

Ideally, misinformation texts should be supportive

of generated misinformation around 500 words by
using a prompt constraint, and filter out misinformation texts with lengths that deviate too much.

Semantic Conflict Deeper knowledge conflict is
caused due to the polysemous and ambiguous semantics of facts within misinformation. That is, entities in different contexts may have the same name
but express different semantic information. To simulate this scenario, we replace the description of

Entailment Checking To ensure that the generated correct evidences are clear enough to support
the corresponding claims, we utilize Natural Language Inference (NLI)2 (He et al., 2023) to determine the semantic relationship between the origin
claim and the corresponding correct evidence. We
finally keep the claim-evidence pairs that both satisfy: (1) correct evidence entails the origin claim;
(2) each misinformation entails the premise itself.

Semantic Matching Validation From a semantic perspective, generated misinformation should
be similar to the query in semantics while presenting conflicting viewpoints. We utilize SentenceTransformer3 (Reimers and Gurevych, 2019) to
generate embeddings for the question and misinformation in each claim-evidence pair and compute
their similarities. Then we filter out those with a

Human Evaluation To robustly assess the quality and validity of misinformation in constructed

We construct M IS B ENCH benchmark following the
above four-step pipeline, containing 431,113 QA
pairs and 10,346,712 evidences (including correct
and misinformation evidences). Figure 3 shows examples of factual misinformation in six styles. We

Evaluation Metrics We narrow down the generation space by converting open-end QA into a
multiple-choice formula, to simplify knowledge
tracing and constrain LLM response patterns. We
employ three metrics to evaluate the behavior and
knowledge preference of LLMs on M IS B ENCH:

How do LLMs discern misinformation?

This section conducts experiments on M IS B ENCH
to investigate the capacities of LLMs in discerning
misinformation. To identify LLM’s internal knowledge, we prompt each LLM with a multiple-choice
question format (correct answer, irrelevant answer,
"Unsure" etc.) without any external evidence. We
regard that LLMs know the fact when they correctly answer the question, otherwise "Unknown".
Thus, according to "Whether LLMs yield memory
knowledge towards misinformation", we conduct
evaluations in two scenarios: 1) LLMs possess
prior factual knowledge supporting the origin claim
co or cm of the provided misinformation; 2) LLMs
lack corresponding factual knowledge about the
origin claim co or cm of provided misinformation.
LLMs are provided with a single piece of misinformation and prompted in a two-choice QA formula.
We report the Success Rate% of LLMs under both
one-hop and multi-hop misinformation.

Method Based on our empirical findings, we
propose Reconstruction to Discriminate (RtD), a
simple yet promising approach to improve LLMs’
capabilities in discerning misinformation. This
method begins by precisely identifying the key
subject entity within the input text, ensuring focused attention on the essential information unit.
Subsequently, the approach taps into authoritative
sources such as Wikipedia4 to gather detailed descriptions of the entity, thus bolstering the model’s
contextual understanding with reliable external
data. Following this, the LLM is prompted to generate supporting evidence about the entity, built upon
the enriched context, which harnesses its ability to
bridge understanding and production seamlessly.
In the final stage, the LLM is tasked with comparing the original text against the generated content,
discerning the more likely source of misinformation through a sophisticated integration of internal
reasoning and retrieved data.

Finding 3: LLMs exhibit more susceptibility to narrative, subjective misinformation in
reasoning-intensive tasks and to formal, objective misinformation in fact-matching tasks.

Experimental Setup We apply RtD to LLaMA38B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma2-9B on M IS B ENCH.
We set a low temperature setting of 0 during generation with a constraint of 512 for output length and
maintain other configurations default for all LLMs.
All experiments are conducted on a single NVIDIA
A800 PCIe 80GB GPU.

M IS B ENCH in Table 4. It is evidenced that RtD
substantially enhances the baseline LLMs’ performance in discerning three types of misinformation.

For instance, the average Success Rate% on onehop based misinformation detection increases from
23.14 to 47.77 on Qwen2.5-7B. Compared to RtD,
simply feeding retrieved descriptions into the context has limited promotion on LLMs, and it is more
effective on semantic misinformation than on factual or temporal misinformation. These results further prove the effectiveness of the aforementioned
findings and the proposed RtD.

Limitations
While previous works have largely focused on detection errors in specific contexts, such as fake news
or rumors, M IS B ENCH takes a broader approach
by including a wide range of emblematic and pervasive types of misinformation, as well as diverse textual styles. While we strive to capture the most representative forms of misinformation, we acknowledge that our dataset may not fully encompass all
possible variations that exist in real-world scenarios. The complexity and evolving nature of misinformation, combined with the vast diversity of
linguistic styles, make it challenging to achieve
complete coverage. Nonetheless, we believe that
the types and styles included in M IS B ENCH are
sufficiently representative to support meaningful
analysis and evaluation, while recognizing the need

Prompt: Polysemous Description Generation
Task: Resolve semantic conflicts in descriptions involving the same terms used for different roles, due
to polysemy. Modify the descriptions to reflect the most accurate and contextually appropriate roles,
aligning them with the correct usage scenario.
Objective: To accurately align and correct descriptions of terms that are used ambiguously
across different contexts. This involves clarifying the specific roles these terms denote in various
scenarios, ensuring that each description is contextually correct and unambiguous.
Example:
Correct Claim: Franck Dupont holds the position of conseiller municipal de Zouafques.
Conflicting Claim: Franck Dupont holds the position of Governor of Taraba State.
Original Description for "Franck Dupont": French politician.
Description for "Governor of Taraba State": Political position in Nigeria.
Task: Modify the description to modify the usage of "Franck Dupont" by aligning it with a role
appropriate for "Governor of Taraba State".
Modified Description for "Franck Dupont": Nigerian politician.
Template for Generating Descriptions:
Correct Claim: {correct_pair}
Conflicting Claim: {conflict_pair}
Original Description for "{subject}": {subject_description}
Description for "{replaced_object}": {object_description}
Task: Modify the description to modify the usage of "{subject}" by aligning it with a role appropriate for
"{replaced_object}".
Modified Description for "{subject}": [Only return the answer]
